primary.title: The Quran
primary.author: Allah (revealed to Muhammad)
primary.rationale: The central religious text of Islam, believed by Muslims to be the word of God revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. It is considered the most important primary source for understanding Muhammad's teachings and the early Islamic community.

primary.title: Hadith Collections (e.g., Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim)
primary.author: Various Companions (compiled by later scholars)
primary.rationale: Collections of sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad, transmitted through chains of narrators. These are crucial for understanding Muhammad's life, practices, and interpretations of the Quran.

primary.title: The Constitution of Medina
primary.author: Muhammad
primary.rationale: An early document outlining the relationship between the emigrants from Mecca, the helpers from Medina, and the Jewish tribes of Medina. It is considered a foundational document of the early Islamic state.

secondary.title: Muhammad: A Biography
secondary.author: Martin Lings
secondary.rationale: A widely respected biography of Muhammad, known for its detailed narrative and reliance on traditional Islamic sources.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Quran
secondary.author: Michael Cook
secondary.rationale: An academic companion offering diverse scholarly perspectives on the Quran, its historical context, and its interpretation, which indirectly sheds light on Muhammad's role.

secondary.title: Muhammad: Prophet of Islam
secondary.author: Huston Smith
secondary.rationale: A concise and accessible scholarly overview of Muhammad's life and the origins of Islam, suitable for introductory research.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources for Muhammad are primarily religious texts and historical accounts compiled by his followers and later scholars. Direct writings from Muhammad himself are scarce and often embedded within these larger collections. Secondary sources offer scholarly analysis and interpretation of these primary materials.
